[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
The National Archives catalogue describes an order sent by Thomas Frankland at English Harbour to the Naval Officer at Antigua on 3 January 1756, directing the discharge of Michael Glasgow and three other men for incompetence and preventing their entry to the yard. This describes the order; it does not prove when the discharge was carried out. The catalogue gives Michael no age, birthplace, family or specific trade.<ref>The National Archives, Discovery catalogue, [https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C8840820 Thomas Frankland to the Naval Officer at Antigua, 3 January 1756], ADM 106/1118/3 (reviewed 12 November 2026); catalogue description, original uninspected.</ref>

His birth, death and family remain unknown. English Harbour is the correspondence context, not a recorded birthplace.

== Research Notes ==
Michael Glasgow ([[Glasgow-1410|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1410)]]), baptised at Irvine in 1712, remains chronologically compatible. Michael Glasgow ([[Glasgow-1416|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1416)]]), born 19 November 1741, would have been fourteen; the catalogue gives neither age nor occupation, so this is not an exclusion. Michael Glasgow ([[Glasgow-1406|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-1406)]]), recorded as an Irvine skinner in 1679, would be very old in 1756 but is not excluded merely from a before-birth bound. No record bridges any of these Irvine men to Antigua. [[Glasgow-3911|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-3911)]] belongs to the sixteenth century and [[Glasgow-3595|Michael Glasgow (Glasgow-3595)]] was born in 1815, concrete chronological conflicts. Keep this documentary account on identity hold; do not create a duplicate live profile.

Reviewed 12 November 2026 from The National Archives official Discovery catalogue/API description. The original manuscript was not inspected; the catalogue reports the item as not digitised and open. Open archival access does not mean online images exist. No live WikiTree or FamilySearch edit, merge or family attachment follows.

The Michael Glasgow in the separate 1797 Portsmouth journal is not identified with this man. The two descriptions do not establish a shared identity or kinship. The 1797 reported age would place that man’s birth around the time of the earlier order.
